records.summary: Eesti Pank's own annual report lists PIMCO as one of the four external asset managers running part of the central bank's investment assets as at 31 December 2019.
records.detail: Eesti Pank's Annual Report 2019, in the chapter 'Financial asset management', states that at the end of 2019 the bank had four external asset managers and that the external asset management programme is based on overlay mandates, the managers expressing most strategies through derivative instruments; additional income from active investment in 2019 was positive, with both Eesti Pank's own portfolio managers and the external managers contributing, and the total return on the bank's investment assets was almost 39 million euros. The report says PIMCO started working with Eesti Pank in 2005. No amount is given for the individual mandate and no share of reserves is stated; the as-at date is 31 December 2019. The document gives no address for the firm, so the head office is left null.
records.source_title: Eesti Pank Annual Report 2019, chapter 'Financial asset management'
records.quote: At the end of 2019, Eesti Pank had four external asset managers. PIMCO started working with Eesti Pank in 2005

records.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
records.name_as_stated: Banca Mondială ... programului Reserves Advisory and Management Program (RAMP)
records.summary: Under a 2017 technical assistance and asset management contract, the World Bank managed a US dollar portfolio of Romania's international reserves for the National Bank of Romania through its RAMP programme during 2023.
records.detail: Banca Națională a României, Raport anual 2023, Note 8 to the audited financial statements ('Plasamente la Banca Mondială'): under the technical assistance and asset management contract signed with the World Bank in 2017, the World Bank continued in 2023 to provide technical assistance to the BNR and to manage the US dollar denominated asset portfolio allocated by the BNR under the Reserves Advisory and Management Program (RAMP). As at 31 December 2023 the placements managed by the World Bank were deposits of 85,083 thousand lei (USD 18,925 thousand) and securities of 2,663,330 thousand lei (USD 592,403 thousand), 2,748,413 thousand lei in total (31 December 2022: 2,710,628 thousand lei). The note adds that they are managed in accordance with the international reserve management policies described in Note 3. No share of total reserves is given, and the document gives no address for the World Bank, so the head office is left null. This is a management mandate, not a training or advisory mention: the Romanian wording is 'să administreze ... portofoliul de active denominat în dolari americani'.
records.source_title: Banca Națională a României, Raport anual 2023, Nota 8 'Plasamente la Banca Mondială'
records.quote: La 31 decembrie 2023, plasamentele administrate de Banca Mondială sunt următoarele

blanks.note: Swiss National Bank, 'Questions and answers on asset management' (snb.ch/en/iabout/assets/id/qas_assets_1), read in full: the SNB confirms external mandates — 'Mandates are awarded to external asset managers, first if there is an efficiency gain in doing so' and 'because they can be used to benchmark internal asset management' — but names no firm, gives no amount and no share. The page also says the SNB's Asset Management division handles the majority of the investments. So external management is certain and the manager is unnamed. Not yet read: the SNB Annual Report / Financial Report chapter on investment and risk control, and the Swiss federal procurement portal simap.ch, which is the obvious next document.

Národná banka Slovenska Annual Report 2020 (nbs.sk/_img/Documents/_Publikacie/AnnualReport/ARNBS20.pdf), Part B chapter 1.3 'Investment portfolio management' plus footnote 3 and the financial-statement notes: NBS states it 'manages its investment portfolios' itself, but holds (a) renminbi through the BISIP CNY, described in footnote 3 as 'an open-ended fund comprising Chinese government bonds and managed by the Bank for International Settlements in Basel' (market value about USD 47 million at end-2020), and (b) an equity portfolio of 'shares in selected exchange-traded funds representing the global equity market' (EUR 236 million at 31 December 2020). The notes carry balance lines 'Participating interests in ETF funds', 'BISIP and ETF funds' and 'Dividends from ETF funds'. This is a fund holding with a named manager (the BIS), which the brief reserves for the owner, so nothing is filed. The note names the fund (BISIP CNY), names its manager (BIS, Basel) and gives a figure (USD 47 million). No other external manager appears anywhere in the report.

Banka Slovenije, 2024 Audited Financial Statements (bsi.si/storage/uploads/00d58892-953b-4975-a24c-10d6ade64fdd/_2024-BS-Audited-Financial-Statements.pdf) downloaded and grepped in full: the sentence the task quotes about a maturity bucket that 'includes holdings in a BIS fund and of equity ETFs' is NOT in this document — 'BIS', 'ETF' and 'exchange-traded' return zero hits. What the audited statements do carry is a foreign-currency asset breakdown with the three lines 'Sight deposits / Debt securities / Investment funds'; an accounting policy that 'Investment funds are valued at market prices on a net basis and not on the basis of the underlying assets, provided that they meet certain predetermined criteria in relation to the level of influence of Banka Slovenije on the day-to-day operations of the fund'; and Note 30, which says income from equity shares and participating interests 'represents the income received from Banka Slovenije's participation in the international financial institutions and from investments in investment funds'. So the audited statements confirm a fund holding but name no fund and no manager. Nothing filed, per the fund-holding rule. The quoted BIS/ETF sentence is presumably in the Annual Report 2024 (bsi.si Letno-porocilo-2024_EN_07_eng-GB_complete.pdf), which was not opened — that is the document to read if the owner wants the exact wording confirmed.

DNB Annual Report 2025 (dnb.nl/media/d0rdiihe/dnb-annual-report-2025.pdf) downloaded and grepped in full: DNB confirms external management of part of its own-account investments but names no manager. The own-account investments section says 'The self-managed foreign currency portfolio ... consists of high-grade government and semi-government bonds' and 'Our participations in equity and corporate bond funds are externally managed'; the accountability tables say 'All external managers report on the Paris Climate Agreement targets' and 'With the external managers of developing-market equities and corporate bonds we discussed reporting according to the guidelines of the Institutional Investor Group on Climate Change'; DNB also refers to 'our first equity mandate' and to 'our V&E manager'. The accounting policies add that 'Marketable investment funds and portfolios that are externally managed and strictly replicate the performance of an index-linked fund are valued at market price'. Grepped for BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, Schroders, RAMP, World Bank and Crown Agents: no hit. So the vein is open but this document closes: the firms exist and are unnamed here. Next documents to try: DNB's responsible-investment / sustainable investment reporting, and the Dutch procurement portal TenderNed.

Banca d'Italia, Relazione sulla gestione e sulla sostenibilità sul 2025, section on gold and foreign reserves and 'Il portafoglio titoli' (copy at dirittobancario.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Relazione-Banca-dItalia-sulla-gestione-e-sulla-sostenibilita-2025.pdf, 599,000 characters, grepped in full): the non-monetary-policy securities portfolio of EUR 150.6 billion at 31 December 2025 is about 80% euro-area government bonds, 'la quota residua è distribuita tra azioni e obbligazioni di società, obbligazioni di enti sovranazionali, quote di OICR ed exchange-traded funds (ETF) di natura azionaria', and footnote 247 adds that investment continued in 'quote di fondi, promossi da società di gestione del risparmio, specializzati nel settore delle piccole e medie imprese italiane e in progetti infrastrutturali'. So fund units and ETFs are held, but no management company, no fund and no external manager is named, and the only hit for 'gestori esterni' in the document is about servicers in securitisations, not reserve management. Grepped BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, Schroders, RAMP: no hit. Not read: the separate Rapporto annuale sugli investimenti sostenibili e sui rischi climatici, which is the next document to open.

Oesterreichische Nationalbank Annual Report 2025 (oenb.at/dam/jcr:f9d61151-6e0c-46d0-a576-02aaf73c3889/ar-2025.pdf, 292,000 characters, grepped in full including the balance sheet and notes): the only external-investment trace is a balance-sheet line 'Equity instruments / Exchange-traded funds (ETFs)' of EUR 9.829 million at end-2025 against EUR 4.000 million a year earlier, plus a valuation policy sentence on 'securities and investment fund shares/units'. No external asset manager, no mandate and no firm is named anywhere; grepped BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, Schroders, RAMP, World Bank, Crown Agents with no hit. Next document if the row is revisited: the separate OeNB financial statements PDF and the Austrian procurement portal.

Banque centrale du Luxembourg, Rapport annuel 2024 (bcl.lu/fr/publications/rapports_annuels/2024/BCL_RAPPORT_ANNUEL_2024_FR.pdf, 487,000 characters, grepped in full) — the relation runs the other way. Section 1.3 on the BCL's portfolios lists its pension fund portfolio, the ECB foreign reserve portfolio it manages, and 'Portefeuilles pour compte de tiers: Dans le cadre d'une coopération, la BCL gère deux mandats de banques centrales étrangères qui ont externalisé une partie de leurs réserves de change. L'un des mandats est en euros et l'autre en dollars' — i.e. the BCL is the manager for two unnamed foreign central banks, not a client. Its own portfolios (a held-to-maturity bond portfolio of EUR 2,373 million, a renminbi portfolio and gold) are described as run by its own portfolio managers ('Niveau 5: les gestionnaires'), and the report names no external manager of BCL assets. Grepped BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, Schroders, RAMP: no hit. Worth noting for another row: the two outsourcing central banks are unnamed here.

Reserve Bank of Australia Annual Report 2025, Part 2 'Our Operations' (rba.gov.au/publications/annual-reports/rba/2025/pdf/rba-annual-report-2025-part-2.pdf, 165,000 characters, grepped in full): section 2.2 'Operations in Financial Markets' says the RBA's own operations include 'managing Australia's foreign exchange reserve assets' and that 'Foreign exchange reserves were managed to achieve the Board's targets for liquid asset holdings and were within predefined limits for market risk'. No external manager, mandate or firm appears; grepped externally managed, external manager, outsourc, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, asset manager with no relevant hit. Part 4 (the audited financial statements) was not opened, so one document of this vein is still untested for AUS.

Sveriges Riksbank Annual Report 2025 (riksbank.se/globalassets/media/rapporter/arsredovisning/engelska/annual-report-2025.pdf, 222,000 characters, grepped in full): the 'Asset management' chapter describes a new framework in which the Executive Board decides the strategic allocation of the gold and foreign exchange reserves and 'also gives a so-called tactical mandate to the Markets Department' — an internal mandate — and nothing else. No external manager is named or implied; grepped externally managed, external manager, outsourc, BlackRock, Amundi, PIMCO, UBS, Wellington, asset manager: the only hits are 'cash management in-house' at Bankomat and in-house IT development. In-house management confirmed for 31 December 2025.

Only one page opened: MAS Annual Report 2021/22 'Reserve Management' (mas.gov.sg/publications/annual-report/2022/annual-report-2021-2022/macroeconomic-and-financial-stability/reserve-management), which says the Official Foreign Reserves are invested in cash, bonds and equities and that the MAS Board approves the investment universe, and contains no sentence about external fund managers and no firm. That is too thin to call a blank. Next documents: the full MAS Annual Report PDF for a recent year (the financial statements and the 'Central Bank Operations' chapter), and the Ministry of Finance page 'Who manages the reserves?' (mof.gov.sg/policies/reserves/who-manages-the-reserves).
